LLM use statement

Source: vignettes/articles/llm-use.Rmd
llm-use.Rmd

cohortflow was developed with substantial help from large language model (LLM) coding assistants. This page says which tools were used, what they were used for, and how their output was checked.

Tools

  • GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code, running Anthropic’s Claude models, from the start of development (April 2026).
  • Claude Code (Anthropic), from August 2026, with Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1.

What the assistants did

The assistants wrote much of the package’s code, unit tests, roxygen documentation, vignettes and articles, and the package logo. They also drafted implementation plans, reviewed code for bugs, and ran the test suite and R CMD check during development.

What the author did

I (Matthew Moore) decided what the package should do: its scope, its interface, and how it should count and report participants. I wrote or approved the plan for each feature before it was implemented, and I reviewed every change before it was merged. I am responsible for all of the package’s contents, including any errors in them.

How the output was checked

  • An automated test suite (testthat) covers the package’s functions, including the counts in attrition tables, diagrams and narrative text. Coverage is tracked on Codecov.
  • Every pull request and push to master runs R CMD check on Linux, macOS and Windows, and lintr, through GitHub Actions.
  • Worked examples in the articles are re-run each time this site is built, so their output comes from the current code.

Data

All example datasets in the package (mock_parallel_rct() and the other mock_*() functions) are synthetic. No real participant or patient data were shared with any AI tool during development.

Tracing AI contributions

Since August 2026, commits made with Claude Code end with a Co-Authored-By: Claude ... trailer, so the commit history shows which changes they were involved in. Earlier commits, made with GitHub Copilot, carry no such marker, so assume that any part of the package may have been written with AI assistance.

If you find a problem, please open an issue.

Last updated: 24 November 2026.
